key_insight: A-site high-entropy disorder combined with tensile strain improves oxygen evolution activity in nickelate thin films, while the high-entropy material resists degradation better than LaNiO3.
engineering_relevance: Joint control of composition and epitaxial strain offers a route to improved oxide electrocatalysts for water electrolysis, rather than solar-cell absorbers.
method: Study epitaxial (La0.2Pr0.2Nd0.2Sm0.2Eu0.2)NiO3 films under different strain conditions.
Probe structural defects, Ni valence, and electronic states using characterization including O K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy.
Combine first-principles calculations with OER activity and degradation comparisons.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports earlier OER onset and higher activity under tensile strain than under compressive strain and in representative single-A-site nickelates, plus improved degradation resistance relative to LaNiO3.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical performance or durability metrics, and scalability beyond epitaxial thin films remains unestablished.
paper_title: High-Entropy A-Site Disorder Enhances Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity and Stability in Nickelate Thin Films
